newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan factions fight for alleged Taleban captives.
newsitem.headline: Afghan factions fight for alleged Taleban captives.

text.p: Afghan opposition forces on Sunday battled a militia that claims to hold up to 800 prisoners from Afghanistan's dominant Taleban movement, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said at least 10 fighters had been killed in heavy fighting, which took place mostly on the outskirts of the opposition-held town of Pul-i-Khumri.
Forces loyal to ousted government military commander Ahmad Shah Masood also attacked Taleban positions in Kapisa province, northeast of Kabul, but were repulsed, AIP said.
A Taleban force fled from Pul-i-Khumri earlier this month and took refuge in Baghlan, 30 km (19 miles) to the north, held by Bashir Baghlani, a commander of the Hezb-i-Islami militia.

Hezb-i-Islami, a mainly ethnic Pashtun force like the Taleban, is officially opposed to the purist Islamic militia which controls the bulk of Afghanistan but has stayed out of a northern opposition alliance.
Anti-Taleban forces, including those of Masood, the Shi'ite Moslem Hezb-i-Wahdat militia and an Ismaili militia led by Syed Jafar Naderi, want Baghlani to hand over his Taleban prisoners.
The opposition alliance accuses Baghlani of supporting the Taleban. He has denied the charge, saying he is holding 700 to 800 Taleban prisoners, along with some of their junior leaders.
However, Taleban leaders have said Baghlani is cooperating with them. There has been no definite word on whether the Taleban who fled to Baghlan were made prisoner or not.
The Taleban, who captured the Afghan capital in September, are trying to impose purist Islamic rule throughout Afghanistan which has been devastated by almost 20 years of war.
